newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police hold 12 over attack on Juppe office.
newsitem.headline: French police hold 12 over attack on Juppe office.

text.p: French police on Thursday detained 12 people in connection with a Corsican guerrilla bomb attack on the mayoral office of Prime Minister Alain Juppe in Bordeaux two weeks ago, the Interior Ministry said.
It said they were held in police swoops in the regions of Bordeaux and Marseille, and in Bonifacio on the French Mediterranean island of Corsica.
Juppe had ordered a crackdown on Corsican separatists who claimed responsibility for the attack which caused no injuries but badly damaged the Bordeaux town hall.
The Interior Ministry gave no details of the arrests which were carried out by a special police squad on orders from the country's senior anti-terrorist investigating judge, Jean-Louis Bruguiere.

The "historic wing" of the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) has claimed responsibility for the Bordeaux bombing, as well as for two later bombings of official buildings in the southern town of Nimes.
The mainland attacks were a big escalation by separatists who had confined their campaign for greater autonomy from France to Corsica for the past few years.
